messages:
jordan: Heads-up — ISP swapped my gateway overnight and now my home server is behind CGNAT. Cameras unreachable and some ports broken. Anyone ran into this after a modem swap?
amy: Which ISP? some of them push carrier-grade NAT on new equipment.
devon: If you suddenly see a 100.64.x.x address that's CGNAT. Quick check: \`curl icanhazip.com\` from the machine.
jordan: Ran that — shows 100.64.45.12. Ugh. Also the new box has no obvious bridge mode. pic: https://img.hosting.example/desk-cable-spaghetti.jpg
sahil: Yep that's CGNAT. Short term: request a public/static IP from the ISP or stick your own router behind theirs and use DMZ. Long term: ask for true bridge/transparent mode.
olga: Another trick is to use an exit node like Tailscale or ngrok for external access if you need reachability fast.
amy: Cameras can often be made happy by forcing 5GHz on the AP or putting them on a separate VLAN, but that won't fix CGNAT.
jordan: Thanks — ordered a tiny travel router to run as the network edge and will set up Tailscale as a fallback. Will post my config later if anyone's curious. Also planning to finally fix the desk cable spaghetti tomorrow :sweat_smile:
devon: Please post the before/after. And the router model — might steal the setup. :grin:
